text: [calm] She does everything.
[softly] And somehow... it's never enough.
[warmly] Six in the morning.
Before anyone else is awake, her day has already begun.
[brisk] Lunchboxes. A project due Friday. The dentist. Homework. Dinner. Laundry.
[proudly] Every box. Every day.
At nine, work.
[proudly] She delivered the project. On time. Every piece.
[disappointed] And still, the first thing she heard was: you missed a part.
At six, homework.
[tired] Fractions. Spelling. One more page.
[sighs] And every single night, an argument.
At seven, dinner.
[hopeful] A new recipe tonight.
[flatly] It's... okay.
[sad] And all she heard was: everything I cook tastes bad.
[quietly] One night, on the laundry room floor,
[sad] she wondered if she was failing at everything.
[gently] But let's turn the pages back. [pause] And read them again.
[warmly] She does everything. [pause] And she is enough.
[reassuring] The missing part was never hers.
Her work was done. Done right.
[tenderly] Her daughter argues with her because she feels safe with her.
Kids who stand their ground at home learn to say no out there.
[warmly] Nine dinners before it: loved.
One recipe. Not her.
[moved] She was never the missing piece.
[warmly] She was the one holding it all together.
[with conviction] You're doing better than you think.
[slowly] [deep, low voice] Keep going.
